newsitem.title: USA: Duke Energy files S.C. restructuring plan.
newsitem.headline: Duke Energy files S.C. restructuring plan.

text.p: Duke Energy Corp said on Tuesday that it had filed a proposal to introduce competition in South Carolina's electricity market.

In a filing with the Public Service Commission of South Carolina, the company said it had proposed that the generation of electricity there be deregulated, while the transmission and distribution of electricity continue to be regulated.
Last May, the commission asked interested parties to file restructuring proposals by June 30.
The commission will schedule hearings on the various plans later in the summer.

"With generation prices unregulated, consumers would then be able to negotiate for the price and terms that best suit their needs -- even to purchase additional services as they wish," Duke Energy president Paul Anderson said.
Under the plan, consumers would purchase electricity directly from a supplier, either through power marketers or brokers or through aggregators, the company added.
